posts.cooked:
Upthread, I suggested an alternate base power: Search your deck or discard pile for PRIDE or PREJUDICE. Put it into play.

There was one reply:

Nielzabub:

That might make her a bit overpowered. Pride and Prejudice by themselves aren't too much, but together they can be quite a handful, and with this power, you could easily have both of them in two turns, and it would make equipment destruction mostly meaningless to Ex-Pat. I agree that Ex-Pat should have a way to more reliably get what she needs whether it's ammo or guns.

I don't think it would make equipment destruction meaningless, because she doesn't have many cards that do damage directly. So if her equipment were destroyed then either (a) she has a gun in hand to play and uses it or (b) she has to skip her card play to use the power, and doesn't get to make an attack on the turn after losing equipment. In the second case, all she has out is Pride or Prejudice - which just does as much damage as the base character powers which do direct damage.

So equipment destruction would slow her down for a turn or two. If the goal is to give her reliable access to guns, I don't see how it could do any more than that.

 

I could imagine not using this power at all in many games, if I had decent cards. It makes her more secure than her usual base power, so give her fewer hit points to compensate.

Let's start with the claim that Expatriette is already powerful enough, so any tweak is just to make her more fun, not more powerful.

Expatriette's base power allows her to play more cards that other heros.  If nothing let's you draw additional cards, you're stuck only being able to use that power 3 times before you've got an empty hand.  There doesn't seem to be much incentive in skipping your turn to draw an additional card, because you loose out on the opportunity to use a power and deal damage.  How do we entice her to skip turns?

I played a game against Citizen Dawn today.  I had some time to kill, and drew Ra, Chrono-Ranger, Tachyon and Expatriette, and thought: "Well, won't this be applicable to the conversation?"  I counted the damage.

The heroes were helped most of the game by Imbued Frailty from the Realm of Discord, which I applied to all of their damage numbers, but I tracked hero-granted buffs in a column special to that hero.  I also counted Expatriette's Nemesis bonus seperately.  

The final number for "real" damage was Expatriette 35, Chrono-Ranger 30, Ra 28, and Tachyon 9.  While Chrono-Ranger and Ra were applying their ridiculous single-target bonuses near the end of the game, Expatriette edged them out due to her multi-targeting nature the whole game.  She was only able to get out the Submachine Gun and Assault Rifle, but these proved more than sufficient for this game.  

The story changes only a little bit when you add the buffs in.  Ra added 9 points of damage with a late Imbued Fire, while Chrono-Ranger's By Any Means was responsible for 4 more damage in his column.  This would appear to pull Ra to a total roughly equivalent with Expatriette, but for this game, her nemesis bonus brought her value up 6 more points.  

Overall, she usually works fine for me.  The lack of card draw is a glaring issue, but it doesn't make her unplayable.

Yes it really does say a lot for her to be last.  Honestly I'm very surprised she ever had more than one target to hit in that scenario, but different people play in different ways.

I'm coming around more and more to her.  I have always thought she was fine IF she could get a good gun early.  The downfall is she doesn't have a consistent way to do that.  I had a game last night where she did quite well (she was first in the order btw).  But I also played bay changing her base power to "do 1 target 1 damage and draw a card".  Turns went like this

1.I put out a hair trigger and used this power.  On my REGULAR draw (second card drawn) I got a quick draw.

2.I played quick draw to put pride into play and used the new power again.  Again I benefitted as on the second card (the one from the normal draw) I got prejudice. 

3.I play predjudice and its bang bang every turn after.  I never used this power again but it was nice to be able to get set up a little faster and do 1 point of damage each turn.  I didn't hit another gun or quick draw till the game was nearly over

If I had played with her normal power it would have been

1.Do nothing draw two and get the quick draw

2.Play hair trigger and use power to play quick draw

3.Maybe I use pride, or I do nothing and draw two

4a.If I had drawn two last time I play predjudice and I'm going one turn and 2 damage later slower than what is stated above.

4b.Or If I had used pride I use it again and draw predjudice

5b.Play predjudice and continue as in real game.

 

In the end I got things going 1 to 2 turns faster and nothing changed after.  The big thing here is it helps to eliminate that bad game where you draw and draw and cant find what you need.  In addition to her guns, lets say I really need an RPG, I really like the chance to do less damage to help me find it faster.
